concerns.title: Jordan Lemmons — XTO, Woodfin-Dollie W16C 3H, 09:45 AM, job 36441. Benzene detected above zero during the wellhead and flow line disconnect. The form records the reading
concerns.text: : "Completed the job we did some some benzene of 0.71 so the mt requested to let it air out and rest so we didn't and got 0s so continued with job and got it finished" The narrative indicates the area was allowed to air out and re-tested to zero before work resumed. Follow-up: confirm with Lemmons that the 0.71 reading and the re-test were logged on the Exxon atmospheric testing log, and that the MT concurred with resuming.

concerns.title: Cindy Smith (1099) — XTO, Woodfin-Dollie W16C 3H, 09:47 AM, job 36442. Same well and same operation as item 1, documented independently by the second technician
concerns.text: : "Work area and bleeder valves tested prior to crew beginning work. Benzene was detected on first and second break but dissipated quickly. Crew was able to work without supplied air. confirm.text: Two items go the other way and are worth raising with the technician. First, Jordan Lemmons (36441) reported benzene at 0.71 in his narrative while selecting only one observation item, "Job scope completed safely and as planned", and no stop-work or unsafe-conditions item. Lemmons appeared on this same inverse pattern on 09/26/2026, when he described two leaking valves on a wellhead disconnect without selecting "Unsafe conditions" — this is a recurrence of the same pattern and is the clearest training item in today's set. Second, Cindy Smith's form on the same well records benzene detected on two consecutive breaks, also without an unsafe-conditions selection. Neither is being reported as a confirmed unsafe condition; both need the technician's confirmation of whether the detection warranted the selection.

Selections appear to be carried forward rather than made fresh. Kirschke's three University 58-17 forms carry an identical nine-item selection string; Flores's three carry an identical seven-item string, and his free-text "What Did We Observe? Continued", "What Went Well? Continued" and Learn fields are word-for-word identical across three different wells. Kirschke's narratives differ form to form; Flores's do not. That is the training point rather than a safety finding.

Air jobs — nothing missing. All five air-job assignments on the Permian board were documented by every assigned technician, and all three trailers met the full daily requirement of two Trailer Inspection Forms plus one Trailer Readiness Form:

Trailer 601 (XTO, University 58-17C 3H / 58-17E 5H / 58-17F 6H; Stefanie Kirschke and Rolando Flores 1099; tickets 102651, 102652, 102653) — Kirschke filed a Trailer Inspection Form at 09:08 AM at the Andrews shop, Flores a second at 04:04 PM at Midkiff, and Flores the Trailer Readiness Form at 06:02 PM. Six air job forms filed, one per technician per well. Complete.

Trailer 602 (XTO, Currie 44H 8H; Andrew Bailey and Joseph Popillion 1099; ticket 102649) — all three trailer forms were filed by Andrew Bailey alone (inspections at 05:40 AM on TX-176 and 12:37 PM at Garden City, readiness at 12:39 PM). That satisfies the requirement, which is counted across the crew — nobody needs to chase Popillion for a trailer form. Both air job forms filed.

Trailer 606 (XTO, Woodfin-Dollie W16C 3H; Jordan Lemmons and Cindy Smith 1099; ticket 102650) — all three filed by Jordan Lemmons alone (inspections at 05:23 AM at the Andrews shop and 09:49 AM at Midkiff, readiness at 11:51 AM). Complete. Both air job forms filed.
Confined space — none ran. Both SM Energy Money Graham CTB confined space rows are marked ON STANDBY on the board, so no documentation was due.
Supervision — eight shifts with no H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection Form received. Full-time employees first:

Dawson Drake — BPX, State Blake 57-T3-46 W104H, workover supervision, ticket 102567, board AT# 504. Drake closed out the supervision job form (36472_1) at 04:04 PM after an overnight pause, but no H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection Form was received for his shift.

Michael Ellis — Machin & Associates, Elliot #1, production supervision, ticket 102360, board AT# 142, night shift. No daily inspection form received. Joshua Blassingame covered days and filed his. Blassingame's own form notes "#6 when Mike Ellis gets here it will be put on a sensor stand", which indicates the night shift was expected to be worked.

Dennis Easley — SM Energy, Cold Snack Fed Com 214H, workover supervision, ticket 102667, board AT# 151. Easley holds two supervision assignments on the same trailer today and filed one daily, naming Schlitz Federal Com 231H. No daily naming Cold Snack Fed Com 214H was received. If one trailer and one technician covering two wells needs only one daily, this is not a gap — worth settling so it stops recurring.

The remaining five shifts belong to 1099 contractors, and it is not yet established whether every 1099 contractor is set up to file in StreetSmart at all, so a form that was never expected is not a form that is missing: Benjamin Boutte 1099 (SM Energy, Junior Mint 223H, nights, AT# 503); Trevor McKenzie 1099 (Ovintiv, UL Cathedral 36, nights, AT# N/A); Don Quisenberry 1099 (Comstock, Seaburgs Pad drillout, nights, AT# 138); and Steve Henson 1099 and Cleveland Broughton 1099 (Comstock, Kretzschmar PBH 1H flowback, days and nights, AT# 130 — no form from either). Boutte has previously appeared for leaving hydro dates and cascade pressure blank; today no form was received from him at all.

Supervision shifts that were covered: Allen White (Comstock, Seaburgs Pad), Joshua Blassingame (Machin & Associates, Elliot #1), Brey Rasco (SM Energy, Junior Mint 223H), Dennis Easley (SM Energy, Schlitz Federal Com 231H), and Marcos Morales 1099 (Ovintiv, UL Cathedral 36 — form received at 6:26 PM but unreadable, so its contents are unverified; the submission itself exists).

Field service — nothing missing. Jordan Lemmons's Ovintiv job 36507 carries a completed "Details if Any" describing the LEL sensor board swap. The work described is not a trailer move or delivery, so no Trailer Inspection Form was required for it.

Five board rows in job types whose documentation requirement is not defined in this review, listed so they are not mistaken for an oversight: Comstock inspections route, Larry Taylor, MULTIPLE LOCATIONS, AT# N/A; Sabine Energy gate guard, Wyatt Pad, Andre Inglis 1099 GG and John Kelly 1099 GG, AT# GGS; and the three Southwest Operating rows at Hughes #1 (HSE / safety, gate guard, traffic control), all AT# N/A, all 1099. No forms were received for any of these.

One open question on trailer coverage. Six trailers appear as AT# on supervision and gate guard rows with no Trailer Inspection Form or Trailer Readiness Form of either kind received today: WTX 503, 504 and 151, and ETX 130, 138 and 142. The daily two-inspections-plus-one-readiness requirement as written attaches to air jobs and confined space jobs, so these are not being reported as gaps. Please confirm whether that requirement extends to supervision assignments with a trailer on location — if it does, these six are missing and should be reported from tomorrow.

Dennis Easley — H2S daily with complete cascade and hydro entries plus supervision job 36344 closed out after four days, the one item being a 12/28/2025 ELSA photo. The six Trailer Inspection Forms were uniformly clean on their own terms: Stefanie Kirschke (trailer 601), Rolando Flores (601), Jordan Lemmons (606, twice) and Andrew Bailey (602, twice) each captu

Trailer forms of both kinds and the equipment sections of the H2S daily are photo-based, so a defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside images, not as text, so they cannot be checked here.

Two further limits apply today. Marcos Morales's H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection Form (6:26 PM, Ovintiv UL Cathedral 36) could not be opened — the PDF is 27.2 MB against a 26.2 MB limit on the mail connector, and it failed on repeated attempts including a paged read. Nothing inside it has been checked: not the FR coveralls answer, not the comments to management, not the equipment items. It is worth opening directly in Outlook. This review ran at 11:00 PM Central, so the usual sweep of the following morning for late-arriving submissions could not be performed, and the latest form in the mailbox arrived at 6:44 PM. Any form submitted this evening that is still in transit is not in this count and will need picking up tomorrow.

32 of 33 submissions read. The job board was available — the 10/31/2026 ArkLaTex and Permian Basin boards from Blake Walton, circulated 9:51 AM, using the "10-31 DRAFT" sheet on both workbooks. Both manned blocks were read in full, giving 25 active assignments checked for coverage after removing rows marked ON STANDBY, DAYS OFF, WTX SUPPORT and leave.
